subproblem.title: Directional derivative of a Lipschitz map along DΦ(w)s equals D(f∘Φ)(w)s (Simon Ch. 2, 4.7/4.10)
subproblem.statement: Let n, P, Q ∈ ℕ, f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Suppose f is K-Lipschitz (K ≥ 0) on some neighbourhood V of Φ(w), Φ is differentiable at w, and f∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) (t ∈ ℝ) has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0, where DΦ(w) = fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) = fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n P Q : ℕ) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (w : Eucl n), (∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (Φ w), LipschitzOnWith K f V) → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w → ∀ s : Eucl n, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w s) 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(f∘Φ)(w) := fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w; “f is K-Lipschitz on V” means |f(y) − f(z)| ≤ K|y − z| for all y, z ∈ V; o(t) denotes a function of t ∈ ℝ that is little-o of t as t → 0.

This is the fact (DD) used in step 5 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule; Simon Ch. 2, 4.7 and 4.10): for small |t| both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |f(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(Φ(w + ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w + ts)| = o(t), while f(Φ(w + ts)) = f(Φ(w)) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t).

Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ and put x := Φ(w), v := DΦ(w)s, b := D(f∘Φ)(w)s, g₁(t) := f(x + t v), g₂(t) := f(Φ(w + t s)) and h := g₁ − g₂ (t ∈ ℝ).

1. (Derivatives along the line.) The affine line ℓ(t) := w + t s satisfies ℓ(0) = w and has derivative s at t = 0. Since Φ is differentiable at w = ℓ(0), the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) shows that t ↦ Φ(w + t s) has derivative DΦ(w)s = v at t = 0. Since f∘Φ is differentiable at w, the chain rule likewise shows that g₂ = (f∘Φ)∘ℓ has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s = b at t = 0.

2. (First-order expansion of Φ along the line.) By step 1 and the little-o characterization of derivatives (hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO), using Φ(w + 0·s) = x: Φ(w + t s) − x − t v = o(t) as t → 0.

3. (Both points eventually lie in V.) As t → 0, x + t v → x (continuity of t ↦ x + t v) and Φ(w + t s) → Φ(w) = x (the map t ↦ Φ(w + t s) is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0). Since V is a neighbourhood of x, there is a neighbourhood of t = 0 on which x + t v ∈ V and Φ(w + t s) ∈ V. For such t, because f is K-Lipschitz on V,
|h(t)| = |f(x + t v) − f(Φ(w + t s))| ≤ K|x + t v − Φ(w + t s)| = K|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|.

4. (h has derivative 0 at 0.) By step 3, h(t) = O(|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|) as t → 0, and by step 2 the latter is o(t); hence h(t) = o(t) (Asymptotics.IsBigO.trans_isLittleO). Moreover h(0) = f(x) − f(Φ(w)) = 0. So h(t) − h(0) − t·0 = o(t), i.e. h has derivative 0 at t = 0 (hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO).

5. (Conclusion.) g₁ = g₂ + h pointwise, since g₂(t) + (g₁(t) − g₂(t)) = g₁(t). By steps 1 and 4 and the sum rule (HasDerivAt.add), g₁ has derivative b + 0 = b at t = 0, that is, HasDerivAt (fun t => f (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w s) 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Chain rule along ℓ(t) = w + ts: t ↦ Φ(w + ts) has derivative DΦ(w)s and g₂(t) = f(Φ(w + ts)) has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0.
For t near 0 both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |g₁(t) − g₂(t)| ≤ K|Φ(w + ts) − Φ(w) − t·DΦ(w)s| = o(t).
h = g₁ − g₂ has h(0) = 0 and derivative 0 at 0, so g₁ = g₂ + h has derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s at 0.

audit.reason: The hypotheses and derivative expressions match exactly. Differentiability supplies the chart-line remainder and the derivative along the chart; the neighbourhood Lipschitz bound makes their image difference little-o. Its value at zero vanishes, so the sum rule proves the claimed derivative without assuming ambient differentiability of f.

Printed source. Simon Ch. 2, 1.2 (Lipschitz extension), 1.4 (Rademacher) and 4.7/4.10 (directional derivatives of Lipschitz maps along curves and lines) supply the printed mathematics for ae_diff_comp and line_deriv_comp.

subproblem.title: Rademacher for f∘Φ: a.e. differentiability of a locally Lipschitz map composed with a C¹ map
subproblem.statement: Let P, Q, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q be locally Lipschitz on U, and let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be of class C¹. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ (Lⁿ = volume): if Φ(w) ∈ U, then f∘Φ is (Fréchet) differentiable at w.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P), IsOpen U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n)), Φ w ∈ U → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ Φ) w
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ, an additive Haar measure on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ. “f is locally Lipschitz on U” (Mathlib LocallyLipschitzOn U f) means: every x ∈ U has a neighbourhood t within U (t ∈ 𝓝[U] x) on which f is K-Lipschitz for some K ≥ 0. Write u := f∘Φ and O := Φ⁻¹(U).

This is step 4 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule): u is locally Lipschitz on the open set O, so covering O by countably many open sets on which u is Lipschitz and applying Rademacher's theorem to Lipschitz extensions shows that u is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. point of O.

1. (O is open.) Φ is C¹, hence continuous, and U is open, so O = Φ⁻¹(U) is open.

2. (u is locally Lipschitz on O.) Let w ∈ O and x := Φ(w) ∈ U.
- Since f is locally Lipschitz on U, there are K₁ ≥ 0 and t₁ ∈ 𝓝[U] x such that f is K₁-Lipschitz on t₁. As U is open and x ∈ U, 𝓝[U] x = 𝓝 x (IsOpen.nhdsWithin_eq), so t₁ is a neighbourhood of x.
- A C¹ map is locally Lipschitz (Mathlib ContDiff.locallyLipschitz), so there are K₂ ≥ 0 and a neighbourhood t₂ of w such that Φ is K₂-Lipschitz on t₂.
- By continuity of Φ at w, Φ⁻¹(t₁) is a neighbourhood of w, hence so is t := t₂ ∩ Φ⁻¹(t₁); in particular t ∈ 𝓝[O] w.
- Φ is K₂-Lipschitz on t and maps t into t₁, where f is K₁-Lipschitz; hence u = f∘Φ is K₁K₂-Lipschitz on t (LipschitzOnWith.comp).
So u is locally Lipschitz on O.

3. (Countable Lipschitz cover.) The sibling lemma countable_lipschitz_cover (Submission.lpf_lli_countable_lipschitz_cover) applied with (P, Q, U, f) := (n, Q, O, u) gives open sets O_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and constants K_i ≥ 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that O ⊆ ⋃_i O_i and u is K_i-Lipschitz on s_i := O_i ∩ O for every i. Each s_i is open, as the intersection of the open sets O_i and O (step 1).

4. (Rademacher on each piece.) Fix i ∈ ℕ. Since u is K_i-Lipschitz on s_i and ℝ^Q is finite-dimensional, there is a Lipschitz map v_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q with v_i = u on s_i (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension; alternatively the componentwise McShane extension x ↦ inf_{y∈s_i}(u^l(y) + K_i|x − y|) of Simon Ch. 2, 1.2). By Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt for the additive Haar measure Lⁿ; SimonGMT Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt), v_i is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ. Let w ∈ s_i be such a point. Since s_i is open, it is a neighbourhood of w on which u = v_i, so u is differentiable at w with the same derivative as v_i (DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence E_i := {w ∈ s_i : u is not differentiable at w} is Lⁿ-null. (Mathlib packages this step as LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem, which gives differentiability of u within s_i at Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ s_i, followed by DifferentiableWithinAt.differentiableAt, valid because s_i ∈ 𝓝 w for w ∈ s_i.)

5. (Conclusion.) E := ⋃_{i∈ℕ} E_i is Lⁿ-null as a countable union of null sets (ae_all_iff). Let w ∉ E with Φ(w) ∈ U. Then w ∈ O ⊆ ⋃_i O_i, so w ∈ O_i for some i, hence w ∈ s_i; since w ∉ E_i, u = f∘Φ is differentiable at w. Hence for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ ℝⁿ, Φ(w) ∈ U implies that f∘Φ is differentiable at w. ∎
proof_key_steps: Φ⁻¹(U) is open, and f∘Φ is locally Lipschitz on it: compose a Lipschitz neighbourhood of f at Φ(w) (U open, so 𝓝[U] = 𝓝) with a Lipschitz neighbourhood of the C¹ map Φ at w.
countable_lipschitz_cover: open O_i with Φ⁻¹(U) ⊆ ⋃ O_i and f∘Φ K_i-Lipschitz on the open sets s_i := O_i ∩ Φ⁻¹(U).

Rademacher on each s_i (Lipschitz extension v_i and LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, packaged as LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem): f∘Φ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. point of the open set s_i.
Countable union over i ∈ ℕ (ae_all_iff); every w with Φ(w) ∈ U lies in some s_i.

audit.reason: Openness converts relative Lipschitz neighbourhoods into ambient ones. Composing local bounds, applying the declared countable-cover dependency, and using Rademacher on each open piece prove precisely the ambient-a.e. implication. No additional chart assumptions or circular results are used.

subproblem.title: Pulling Hⁿ-a.e. properties of M ∩ Φ(Ω) back to Lⁿ-a.e. parameters of an antilipschitz chart
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be (Borel) measurable, and let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be (Borel) measurable with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω, for some c > 0. Let p be any property of points of ℝ^P that holds at Hⁿ-a.e. point of M ∩ Φ(Ω) (∀ᵐ x for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))). Then Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable (Lⁿ = volume), and p(Φ(w)) holds for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) (∀ᵐ w for Lⁿ⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (p : Eucl P → Prop), MeasurableSet Ω → Measurable Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → NullMeasurableSet M (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M ∩ Φ '' Ω)), p x) → NullMeasurableSet (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M) (volume : Measure (Eucl n)) ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), p (Φ w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k) with norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure) on ℝ^P; Lⁿ = volume on ℝⁿ. For a measure μ and a set A, μ⌞A = μ.restrict A, and “q holds μ⌞A-a.e.” means ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), q x. Write S := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M).

This is steps 1–3 of the parent proof (lpf_chart_chain_rule): Hⁿ-null exceptional sets in M ∩ Φ(Ω) pull back to Lⁿ-null sets of parameters, and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable, so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))-a.e. statements become Lⁿ⌞(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M))-a.e. statements.

0. (Null sets pull back.) Fix c > 0 with c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω. The sibling lemma chart_preimage_null (Submission.lpf_raf_chart_preimage_null) applied to (P, n, Φ, Ω, c) gives:
(N) for every Z ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(Z) = 0, Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.

1. (S is Lⁿ-null-measurable.) Since M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, there is a measurable set B ⊆ M with B = M Hⁿ-a.e. (Mathlib NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq); in particular Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0 (ae_eq_set). Because B ⊆ M,
S = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B)):
if w ∈ S and Φ(w) ∈ B, then w lies in the first set; if w ∈ S and Φ(w) ∉ B, then Φ(w) ∈ M ∖ B and w lies in the second set; conversely both sets are contained in S because B ⊆ M and M ∖ B ⊆ M. The first set is measurable, since Ω and B are measurable sets and Φ is a measurable map. The second set has Lⁿ-measure 0 by (N) with Z := M ∖ B. The union of a measurable set and an Lⁿ-null set is Lⁿ-null-measurable (MeasurableSet.nullMeasurableSet, NullMeasurableSet.of_null, NullMeasurableSet.union). Hence S is Lⁿ-null-measurable; this is the first conjunct.

2. (The exceptional set in ℝ^P is Hⁿ-null.) Let Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ¬p(x)} ∩ (M ∩ Φ(Ω)). The hypothesis ∀ᵐ x ∂(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω))), p x says exactly (Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)))({x : ¬p(x)}) = 0 (ae_iff). For every measure μ and all sets s, t one has μ(t ∩ s) ≤ (μ⌞s)(t), with no measurability assumption on s or t (Mathlib Measure.le_restrict_apply). With s := M ∩ Φ(Ω) and t := {x : ¬p(x)} this gives Hⁿ(Z) ≤ 0, so Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

3. (The exceptional set of parameters is Lⁿ-null.) By (N), Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0. Let w ∈ S with ¬p(Φ(w)). Then w ∈ Ω, Φ(w) ∈ M, Φ(w) ∈ Φ(Ω) because w ∈ Ω, and ¬p(Φ(w)); hence Φ(w) ∈ Z and w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z). Thus {w : ¬(w ∈ S → p(Φ(w)))} = {w : w ∈ S ∧ ¬p(Φ(w))} ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z), so this set is Lⁿ-null by monotonicity (measure_mono_null), i.e. ∀ᵐ w ∂Lⁿ, w ∈ S → p(Φ(w)) (ae_iff).

4. (Conclusion.) Since S is Lⁿ-null-measurable (step 1), for every property q one has (∀ᵐ w ∂(Lⁿ⌞S), q(w)) ⟺ (∀ᵐ w ∂Lⁿ, w ∈ S → q(w)) (Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'₀). Applying this with q(w) := p(Φ(w)) to step 3 gives ∀ᵐ w ∂(Lⁿ⌞S), p(Φ(w)), the second conjunct. ∎

(Remark: the null-measurability of S from step 1 is what makes step 4 valid; for a non-measurable S the measure Lⁿ⌞S need not be concentrated on S.)
proof_key_steps: chart_preimage_null: every Hⁿ-null Z ⊆ ℝ^P has Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = 0.
Choose a measurable B ⊆ M with Hⁿ(M ∖ B) = 0; Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) = (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B)) ∪ (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M ∖ B)) is measurable ∪ Lⁿ-null, hence Lⁿ-null-measurable.
{w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) : ¬p(Φ w)} ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z) is Lⁿ-null, and ae_restrict_iff'₀ (using null-measurability) turns this into the restricted a.e. statement.
